corpus_definition: a light knock; also a device that controls water flow

forms.definition: a quick light hit, often with your finger
forms.example: I felt a tap on my shoulder.

syn.note: A hit on a door or surface, often louder.

forms.definition: a thing you turn to let water come out
forms.example: Turn off the tap when you brush your teeth.
forms.note: A different meaning: the water device, not a light knock.

forms.definition: to hit something quickly and lightly
forms.example: She tapped gently on the door.

syn.note: Hit a door to ask to come in.
Touch gently with a flat hand.

context.text: Nodira tapped on the window to wake her brother. After the third tap, he finally opened his eyes.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: definition mixes two meanings; the knock sense is used here, the water tap is other_meaning.

corpus_definition: How hot or cold something is.

forms.definition: how hot or cold something or someone is
forms.example: The temperature is rising today.

syn.note: Related: how hot something is, not how cold.

forms.note: 'have a temperature' = be ill with a fever.

context.text: In July the temperature in Tashkent can reach forty degrees. Doctors tell people to drink a lot of water when temperatures are so high.

reviewer_note: No family forms in learner use.

corpus_definition: A period of time during which school takes place.

forms.definition: one of the periods of the school or university year
forms.example: The school term ends in June.

syn.note: One of two parts of the school year, common in American English.

ant.note: Time when there is no school.

forms.definition: a word or phrase with a special meaning
forms.example: "Gravity" is a scientific term.
forms.note: A different meaning: a word, not a school period.

forms.definition: to call something by a particular name
forms.example: This style is termed modern.
forms.note: Belongs to term = a word or name. Formal.

context.text: The new term starts in September. In the first term, Sardor wants to study harder.

reviewer_note: termly (adjective/adverb) is rare British English, so no_form.

corpus_definition: An idea or opinion in your mind.

forms.definition: an idea or opinion in your mind
forms.example: I had a sudden thought about the trip.

forms.definition: to have an idea or opinion in your mind
forms.example: I think it will rain.

forms.definition: kind and thinking about what other people need
forms.example: It was thoughtful of you to bring flowers.
forms.note: Belongs to thought = care for others, not one idea.

forms.definition: in a quiet way, thinking carefully
forms.example: He looked thoughtfully out of the window.

people.definition: a person who thinks seriously about ideas
people.example: Ibn Sina was a great thinker.

context.text: A thought came to Malika on the bus. She thought about it all day and then told her teacher.

reviewer_note: thought is also the past form of think.

corpus_definition: To put something in the trash because you do not need it.
particle_note: Separable: 'throw the paper away' or 'throw away the paper'. With a pronoun, it must go in the middle: 'throw it away'.

relations.note: Remove something you do not want.
Formal word for throwing something away.
Informal British English: put in the bin.
Not throw away; still have it.

context.text: Please do not throw away the old newspapers. Grandpa uses them, so he never throws them away.

reviewer_note: In British English the bin is where you throw things away.

corpus_definition: the loud rumbling sound heard during a storm

forms.definition: the loud noise you hear in a storm after lightning
forms.example: Thunder woke the children in the night.

syn.note: Related: the flash of light, not the sound.

forms.definition: to make the loud noise of a storm
forms.example: It thundered all night.

forms.definition: (of weather) with thunder or likely to have thunder
forms.example: Expect thundery showers this afternoon.

forms.definition: extremely loud, like thunder
forms.example: There was thunderous applause.

syn.note: So loud you cannot hear anything else.

people.definition: a storm with thunder and lightning
people.example: We stayed inside during the thunderstorm.

context.text: We heard thunder all night in our village. It was thunderous, and the dog hid under the bed.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows (B2, A2) merged; A2 used.

corpus_definition: Keeping things clean and in their proper places.

forms.definition: the quality of being neat and in order
forms.example: Her tidiness surprised her parents.

forms.definition: to make a place neat by putting things in order
forms.example: I tidied my desk this morning.

syn.note: Remove dirt; tidy means put things in order.
Put things in a neat order.

forms.definition: neat, with everything in its place
forms.example: Please keep your room tidy.

forms.definition: in a neat way
forms.example: Put your clothes away tidily.

context.text: Aziza is always tidy. She tidies her room every morning and folds her clothes tidily.

reviewer_note: British English uses tidy more than American English.

corpus_definition: To put things back in their proper places.
particle_note: Separable: 'tidy up your room' or 'tidy your room up'. Also used without an object: 'Let's tidy up.'

relations.note: Make a place clean and in order.
Put things back where they belong.

context.text: Please tidy up your room before playing. When the children tidied up, the floor was clear again.

corpus_definition: fixed firmly in place or fitting very closely to the body.

forms.definition: the feeling or state of being tight
forms.example: I felt a tightness in my chest.

forms.definition: to make something tighter or more firm
forms.example: Tighten your seat belt.

forms.definition: fitting very closely, or fixed firmly
forms.example: These jeans are too tight for me.

forms.definition: in a firm, close way
forms.example: Hold the rope tightly.

syn.note: Strongly, so it does not move.

context.text: My new shoes are too tight. I tied the laces tightly, and now my feet hurt.

corpus_definition: A metal container used for holding food or drinks.

forms.definition: a closed metal container for food
forms.example: She opened a tin of beans for lunch.

syn.note: Same meaning; more common in American English.

forms.definition: a soft silver-white metal
forms.example: The roof is made of tin.
forms.note: The metal itself, not the container.

forms.definition: kept in a metal container
forms.example: We bought tinned tomatoes.

ant.note: Not kept in a tin; recently picked or made.

context.text: Grandma keeps tinned fish in the cupboard. She opens a tin when guests arrive.

reviewer_note: tin = container is British English; can is American.
